newsitem.title: UK: Kenyan T-bills have short-term attraction-M.Lynch.
newsitem.headline: Kenyan T-bills have short-term attraction-M.Lynch.

text.p: Kenyan three-month Treasury bills offer a lucrative return but the chances of the currency remaining stable in the second half of the year are less certain, Merrill Lynch said on Thursday.
"The bills, which most recently yielded 21.45 percent, offer attractive returns of about 18.5 percent net of withholding tax," Merrill's analyst Eric Lindenbaum said in a research report.
He expected the Kenyan shilling to be stable at around 55 to the dollar in the first half of the year.
"We are more cautious about the currency in the second half of the year as election jitters could lead to a slowdown in short term capital flows," he said.
Kenyan President Daniel arap Moi and his KANU party are expected to remain in power and there is unlikely to be a repeat of the spending spree that came with the 1992 election.

Kenya has made significant progress in macroeconomic stabilisation and the current account is likely to be near balance for the year with high interest rates on T-bills continuing to attract short-term capital inflows, he said.
He estimated the country's rating, were it to get one, would be around B plus.
